extracted_concepts.name: Product Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Rule for differentiating the product of two or more differentiable functions

extracted_concepts.name: Quotient Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Rule for differentiating the quotient of two differentiable functions where the denominator is non-zero

extracted_concepts.name: Differentiable function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A function that has a defined derivative at every point in its domain

extracted_concepts.name: Leibniz notation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Notation using d/dx to represent derivatives, e.g., d/dx(uv)

extracted_concepts.name: Derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The instantaneous rate of change of a function with respect to its variable

extracted_concepts.name: First derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The initial derivative of a function, denoted as f'(x) or df/dx

extracted_concepts.name: Second derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The derivative of the first derivative, denoted as f''(x) or d²f/dx²

extracted_concepts.name: Higher-order derivatives
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Successive derivatives beyond the second order, such as f'''(x) or f⁽⁴⁾(x)

extracted_concepts.name: Position
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The location of an object as a function of time, typically denoted s(t)

extracted_concepts.name: Velocity
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The first derivative of position with respect to time, representing rate of motion

extracted_concepts.name: Acceleration
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The second derivative of position with respect to time, representing rate of change of velocity

extracted_concepts.name: Jerk
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The third derivative of position with respect to time, representing rate of change of acceleration

extracted_concepts.name: Exponential function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A mathematical function of the form e^x commonly used in calculus examples

extracted_concepts.name: Sine function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A trigonometric function sin x frequently differentiated using calculus rules

extracted_concepts.name: Polynomial term
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Algebraic expressions like x² used in differentiation practice problems

extracted_concepts.name: Denominator square
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The squared denominator g(x)² appearing in the quotient rule formula

extracted_concepts.name: Mnemonic phrase
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Memory aid 'Low d-high minus high d-low, all over the square of what's below' for the quotient rule

extracted_concepts.name: Differentiation operator
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The symbolic operator d/dx applied to functions to compute derivatives

extracted_concepts.name: Prime notation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Notation using primes (') to denote derivatives, e.g., f'(x) and u'

extracted_concepts.name: Extended product rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Generalization of the product rule to three or more functions: d/dx(uvw) = u'vw + uv'w + uvw'

extracted_concepts.name: Time-dependent function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A function s(t) where the independent variable represents time in physical contexts

extracted_concepts.name: Rate of change
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The fundamental meaning of a derivative in both mathematical and physical applications

extracted_concepts.name: Calculus rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Formulas governing differentiation operations including product and quotient rules

extracted_concepts.name: Function division
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The operation of dividing one differentiable function by another, requiring the quotient rule

extracted_concepts.name: Function multiplication
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The operation of multiplying two differentiable functions, requiring the product rule
